data.outcome_summary: The OECD PISA 2022 factsheet for Greece summarizes how 15-year-old students performed in mathematics, reading and science, and how results changed relative to earlier cycles (notably 2018 and 2012). It reports mean performance trends, proficiency-level distributions (e.g., Level 2 and Level 5/6), and gaps by student subgroups such as socio-economic status (ESCS quintiles), gender, and immigrant background. For Greece, average performance declined in all three subjects between 2018 and 2022, and the share below Level 2 increased in mathematics, reading and science. The factsheet also highlights within-country inequality patterns (e.g., ESCS-related gaps in mathematics) and contextual factors (e.g., teacher support, disciplinary climate, belonging, safety, parental involvement) alongside COVID-related schooling experiences. Estimates are presented with uncertainty (95% confidence intervals), and the note states that Greece met PISA quality standards for reporting in 2022.
